lexicon_entries.comment_en: Preposition with the dative; in, within. Temporal in 1:1; relational context requires care in 1:4.
Beginning; dative singular here. The phrase invites comparison with Genesis 1:1, without establishing direct textual dependence.

Be; ἦν is imperfect third-person singular in the comparison text. Sinaiticus transcription v1.95 reports unaccented εϲτιν at John 1:4, here editorially normalized ἐστίν (present third-person singular). Tense interpretation and clause attachment require separate textual analysis.
Definite article; inflection and syntactic function vary. Article presence and absence require contextual analysis.
Word, discourse, account; used as a designation in this passage. Capitalization belongs to the digital edition.
Coordinating conjunction, normally and here; discourse function must be assessed locally.
Preposition with the accusative here; relation or orientation toward. Do not substitute a theological paraphrase for a lexical account.

God or deity according to context; accusative and nominative forms here. Predicate syntax at 1:1 must be distinguished from lexical meaning. Bezae 1.03 preserves the contracted nomina sacra θν and θς; their assignment to this lemma is contextual and does not replace the source abbreviations.
Demonstrative pronoun, nominative masculine singular; refers back within the preceding discourse.
All; neuter plural here. Its syntactic relation to the verb should be stated separately from its semantic scope.
Preposition, elided before a vowel; with genitive here, through. Retain source elision and apostrophe.
Pronominal forms; genitive, dative, and accusative here. Referents require contextual resolution.

Become, come into being, happen; aorist and perfect forms here. Clause attachment at 1:3–4 remains under review. Bezae 1.03 at John 1:3 n=8 transcribes ενεγετο. Its tentative assignment here treats the letters as a transposition by context; the transcription is retained unchanged and the interpretation requires review. A source-guided enlarged-image comparison agrees with the sequence ΕΝΕΓΕΤΟ; this does not independently establish its linguistic interpretation.
Apart from, without; governs a genitive expression here.
Negative connective, not even or nor according to syntax; interacts with the following numeral.
One; neuter singular here. Distinguish this numeral from the preposition ἐν despite accent-stripped search-key collision.
Relative pronoun, neuter singular here; its clause attachment requires review of punctuation and interpretation.
Life; nominative singular. The contextual sense requires discussion beyond a one-word gloss.
Light; neuter noun. Distinguish imagery, contextual reference, and lexical meaning.
Human being; genitive plural here. Translation choices depend on referential scope.
Darkness; dative and nominative singular here. Figurative interpretation is contextual.
Shine or appear; present active third-person singular, intransitive use here.
Negative particle; negates the finite verbal assertion here.
Seize, overtake, or grasp according to context; aorist active third-person singular. The rendering in 1:5 is disputed and needs sourced review.

No one, nothing, according to gender and context; neuter singular οὐδέν here. The Sinaiticus transcription encodes ουδεν as the original reading in John 1:3 and ουδε εν in a correction labeled ca. The readings differ in their encoded letters as well as segmentation; do not describe this as spacing alone. No image-level intervention is inferred. Bezae 1.03 also segments ουδεν as one word at John 1:3 n=18. The letters were checked on folio 104v; the word division remains the transcribers’ analysis of scriptio continua.
